models.model_description:
Current-state master record of every CommerceMerchant on the Wish marketplace. One row per merchant: the Mongo `ObjectId` hex string in `id` is the primary key and the view applies `ROW_NUMBER()` de-duplication, so `id` is unique here. The underlying physical object `wish.commerce_merchant` is a Hive VIEW over the MongoDB `sweeper` collection `CommerceMerchant`, refreshed daily at 00:00 UTC by the Airflow DAG `CommerceMerchantDump`.
The table is NOT partitioned and carries no snapshot-date column (no `updated_at` in the schema), so this model has no partition time dimension. The default `agg_time_dimension` is `approved_calendar_date` -- the merchant approval day -- which is a COHORT anchor, not a snapshot day: grouping by it answers "merchants approved that day". Merchants that are not approved yet have a NULL approval date and are therefore dropped from a time-bucketed query. Use `first_transaction_calendar_date` (merchant activation cohort), `last_payment_calendar_date` (disbursement cohort) or `disable_calendar_date` when that is the intent.
This is a merchant dimension, not an event log: every row carries the merchant's state as of the last successful daily dump. Merchant counters (`rating_count`, `num_active_products`, `num_last_90_day_transactions`, `num_disputes_attention`, `num_noti_attention`, `actions_received`) are as-of-dump snapshots and are NOT additive over time -- summing them across dates double counts the same merchant.
Rating metrics (`average_rating`, `rating_count`) are merchant-quality attributes; `rev_share` is a rate (0.0-1.0) and must be averaged, not summed.
Data quality: `is_cost_based` is overwritten by the extract with 'False' for every row and does not reflect the Mongo value; `payment_withhold_until` may hold the application sentinel 3000-01-01 (a far-future / permanent-style hold).
PII columns (`display_name`, `display_name_en`, `name`, `phone_number`, `sales_rep_name`, `close_account_email_code`) are exposed by the underlying view but are deliberately not exposed as MetricFlow dimensions in this semantic model.
Source: documentation/llm_generated/hive/wish/commerce_merchant.md

models.model_description:
Commerce (buyer) refund line items. Grain is one row per `CommerceTransactionRefundItem` — a refund line embedded under a MongoDB `CommerceTransactionRefund` document keyed by `(transaction_id, variation_id)`. `refund_id` is the unique row key; one parent refund document may carry many refund items, so aggregate at `refund_id` before joining to avoid fan-out.

This is the primary analytical source for how much was refunded to the user, by which payment method (original payment vs Wish Cash), why (reason / high-level category), who initiated the refund, and how merchant cost responsibility is allocated. It separates user-facing refund amounts (`amount`, `refund_payment_amount`, `refund_cash_amount`, `refund_fee_amount`) from merchant cost basis fields (`cost`, `shipping_cost`, `merchant_responsibility`, `merchant_tax_amount`) — the two are not interchangeable.

Built daily by Airflow DAG `IncrementalCTRefund_Tahoe` (08:00 UTC): the extract picks refund items whose ObjectId falls in the run-day window, merges them with the prior master, writes a dated snapshot `sweeper_dev.commerce_transaction_refund_items_YYYYMMDD`, and recreates the Hive view `wish.commerce_transaction_refund_items` as `SELECT *` from that snapshot. Partitioned by `dt` (varchar YYYY-MM-DD, Pacific refund-day derived from `refund_time`); always filter `dt` for pruning and for refund-day semantics.

Time semantics: `dt` is the Pacific refund day and is the default metric time dimension. `refund_time` is the refund item creation instant (unix seconds, UTC) and `merchant_payment_time` is the merchant payout deduction instant (stringified unix seconds); both are exposed as timestamp columns for joins only, not as MetricFlow time dimensions (the project time spine is day). `time` and `date` are ETL load-window markers and must not be used for refund reporting.

Known gaps carried from the source: `reason_id` has no name column because `sweeper_dev.dim_refund_reasons` may lag the Python enum — use `reason_id` + `high_level_refund_category` here and join the dimension in a Tableau model. `cash_refund_status`, `credit_refund_status` and `refund_credit_amount` exist on Mongo but are not exported to this table.

models.model_description:
Daily product-level performance fact for commerce engagement and monetization signals. One row per (product_id, dt) per Airflow load cycle of the `DailyCommerceProductMetrics` DAG (daily at 01:00 America/Los_Angeles, covering the previous business-day aggregation window). Consolidates contest impressions, feed-tile and cart-page impressions, exploration traffic, click interactions, WE-scoped signals, purchases and GMV for a product-day.

The physical Hive table declares no primary key. The wrapper exposes the surrogate `product_day_key` (product_id + dt) as the primary entity. `dt` is the partition column, cast to `date` for MetricFlow time semantics, and is the default metric time dimension; it holds the Pacific-time business date of the upstream aggregation window (DAG run date minus one day), not an event timestamp.

Reading notes. Bot filtering, HTTP response-status filtering, excluded transaction states (0 PENDING, 4 DECLINED, 5 REFUNDED, 10 EXCEPTION, 12 REQUIRE_REVIEW) and China-IP traffic exclusion are already applied upstream, so these columns are not raw event counts and must not be compared against unfiltered logs. `purchases` is a summed item quantity, not an order or transaction count. `gmv` and `we_gmv` are physical `bigint` columns, so the stored amounts carry no currency decimals. `we_impressions` and `we_gmv` are WE-scoped subsets of `impressions` and `gmv` and must be read as scoped signals rather than global totals. Rows are only written when the product cleared the upstream inclusion gate (`impressions > 10` or any of wishes / add_to_carts / recommends / product_views / cart_impressions / purchases present), so the row count measures coverage, not the size of the product catalogue.

This table has no user dimension, so buyer- or user-level metrics are not derivable here. Dimension joins (product, merchant, category) belong in a Tableau datasource model that `ref()`s this Hive wrapper, not in this model.

models.model_description:
One row per logged product-rating event, from the Hive table `wish.daily_product_feedback_rating` (schema `wish`, partitioned by a single PACIFIC business date `dt`).
This is an EVENT LOG, not a snapshot of current ratings. The rating API logs one record every time a `ProductRating` document is created or edited, so the same rating identity (`_id`, and logically `(transaction_id, product_id)`) can appear many times over time — for edits, or for `mark_as_fake`. A plain row count therefore over-counts "reviews": use `distinct_ratings` (deduplicated rating documents) or `distinct_rating_identities` (deduplicated `(transaction_id, product_id)` reviews) for review counts, and `MAX_BY(rating, time)` style logic for "current rating per key" questions, which this semantic model cannot express directly.
`dt` is the PACIFIC business date (America/Los_Angeles), derived at load from the event timestamp, and is the default metric time. The sibling table `sweeper.product_feedback_rating` uses a UTC `dt` instead — do not mix the two. `dt_utc` / `hr_utc` are the UTC lineage keys of the upstream sweeper partition and exist for audit only.
`time` is the per-event log timestamp in epoch SECONDS, attached by the Tahoe ingestion pipeline rather than by the rating payload, and is the canonical sort key for "most recent logged event".
Trust filtering mirrors production: keep `likely_fake = 'false'` and, for first-submission metrics, `edit = 'false'`.

models.model_description:
Daily fact table of merchant ERP (third-party platform) API activity. Each daily load captures the DEDUPLICATED combinations of merchant, ERP partner, API event, HTTP response, endpoint URI and application error code for merchant API requests that were made through an ERP partner OAuth application (`partner_id` is not null). One row per (dt, merchant_id, partner_id, tid, response_status, uri, code) tuple -- repeated identical calls inside one day collapse into a single row, so `COUNT(*)` is NOT request volume. The physical object `wish.erp_daily_dump` is written daily at 00:00 UTC by the Airflow DAG `DailyERPDumpTahoe` from `sweeper.merchant_requests` and is partitioned by `dt` (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC).
Time semantics: `dt` is the only business day on the table and the default `agg_time_dimension`. `stat_date` and `time` are unix epoch seconds of the batch start, are identical to each other and to the `dt` day, and are therefore kept as plain columns for epoch-window filters rather than registered as time dimensions. The per-request clock time is NOT on this table -- query `sweeper.merchant_requests` for sub-day analysis or request counts.
Use this model to answer "did merchant X use ERP partner Y for event Z on day D" and to roll up ERP API errors by partner, event, HTTP status or application error code. Use `analytics.erp_client_id_mapping_dump` (joined in a Tableau model, not here) for authoritative partner display names, and `sweeper.merchant_requests` for call volume and latency.
Source: documentation/llm_generated/hive/wish/erp_daily_dump.md

models.model_description:
Consolidated Wish transaction fact — commerce transaction, merchant transaction and order tracking information joined into one fact table. Physical source is the Hive table `wish.fact_trans_detail`, produced daily by the Airflow / Spark ETL (DAG `IncrementalFactTransDetail`, 06:00 PST) that lands the MongoDB `commerce_transaction` / `commerce_transaction_item`, `MerchantTransaction` and `OrderTrackingInfo` documents. This model is a read-only view over that table (materialized in schema `semantic_dw`); the ETL is not reimplemented here.

**Grain** — one row per commerce line item. The documented composite key is (c_transaction_id, variation_id) — the data-quality duplication check for this table dedups on exactly that pair — so the surrogate primary key `transaction_variation_id` is `concat(c_transaction_id, '-', variation_id)`. The table documentation names `c_transaction_id` alone as the primary key, but the table holds several line rows per transaction, so `c_transaction_id` is not unique here.

**Order vs line grain** — one commerce transaction spans many line rows, so the transaction-level columns (`total_amount`, `subtotal`, `total_shipping`, `flat_rate_shipping`, `tax_amount`, `tax_cost`, `tax_fee`, `processor_fee`, `cash`, `discount_amount`, `discounts_applied`, `total_credits_applied`, `credits_applied`, `installments`) are *repeated on every line row* of the same transaction. Summing them over line rows over-counts by the number of lines per transaction; aggregate at `c_transaction_id` first when a per-transaction number is needed. The line-level columns (`paid_price`, `paid_shipping`, `item_price`, `item_total`, `price`, `shipping`, `quantity`, `gmv`, `paid_amount`, `cost`) are safe to sum over line rows.

**Time** — `dt` is the Hive partition (varchar YYYY-MM-DD) and the default metric time dimension; it is the UTC calendar date of the transaction, not the payment-received, order-approved or refund day. `transaction_date`, `payment_received_date`, `order_approved_date`, `order_date`, `confirmed_delivered_date` and `refunded_date` are extra day-grain time dimensions derived from the unix-second columns; the project time spine is day, so no hour/second-grain time dimension is registered. The raw unix columns and their `*_ts` timestamp companions are kept alongside for joins.

**Enums** — `state`, `payment_type`, `client`, `refund_reason_category` and `order_state` keep their raw code column and gain a human-readable `*_name` column built from the documented code list. `app_type_name` already exists in the source and is passed through.

**Caveats** — monetary columns are in the currency named by `currency` (multi-currency rows exist, so cross-currency sums need an exchange-rate aware metric); `is_testing` rows are QA data and should be excluded from production reporting; `ip_address`, `shipping_recipient`, `device_id`, `req_visitor_id` and `seed_visitor_id` are PII; duplicate `c_transaction_id` records occasionally appear because of upstream ETL issues.

**Scope** — the dbt wrapper exposes the full physical column set, while this semantic model surfaces a curated set of dimensions (documented enums, meaningful flags, geography and product attributes) plus the measure columns the metrics aggregate over.

models.model_description:
Cleaned, normalized feed-tile interaction detail for Wish consumer surfaces (home, express, wishlist, search, categories, collections and other discovery surfaces). Grain is one row per product tile interaction: the upstream hourly DAG explodes a single logged event from `sweeper.feed_tile_interactions` into one detail row per product tile, so one logged event can produce many detail rows.
Carries the interaction itself (`action` — impression, clicked, add_to_wishlist, remove_from_wishlist, add_to_cart), the user and session context, the feed / page / module attribution, the Product Boost revenue fields and the quality flags (`likely_bot`, `is_temporary_user`).
Written hourly by the `FeedTileInteractionsCleanHourly_v0` DAG (full `INSERT OVERWRITE` of the hourly partition) and replayed by the `BackfillFeedTileInteractionsDetail_v2` backfill DAG. Partitioned by `dt` (varchar YYYY-MM-DD) and `hr` (integer 0-23), both in US/Pacific — the partition is a Pacific ingest day, while every timestamp column is a UTC epoch value.
The upstream table enforces no key: the ETL dedups the source on `uuid`, which is not carried into the detail table, and the data explosion multiplies each source record. The wrapper therefore exposes the surrogate key `feed_tile_interaction_id`, built from every identifying column that survives the ETL. It is null-free and unique for all practical purposes, but it is not a stable event UUID.

models.model_description: WishPost logistics profit-and-loss (P&L) rollup. Daily snapshot grain at (dt, date_type, date_value, delivery_program, country, region, is_124). models.model_description:
WishPost logistics finance **sales** revenue breakdown over a rolling ~1-year window. Daily snapshot grain at (dt, date_type, date_value, country, region, is_124, business_type, pricing_channel, channel) per aggregation cell. Produced by the `WishpostOverallFinancePNL` Airflow DAG (task `FinanceSalesBreakdownTask`, daily 10:00 Asia/Shanghai) with `INSERT OVERWRITE ... PARTITION (dt='{biz_date}')`, where biz_date = execution_date − 1 day. Each `dt` partition holds a full rolling ~366-day recompute of the sales side, so `dt` is the daily snapshot ("as of") date and `date_value` (exposed as `sales_day`) is the business sales-payment calendar day inside that window. `date_type` is always `sales_date` on this table — the sibling `wishpost.finance_monthly_profits_1y` carries both `sales_date` and `purchase_date` perspectives, this one is sales-side only.
Fee components: `logistics_fee` (sales fee_type 102), `overtime_fine` (fee_type 108, a fee amount and NOT a timestamp), `sensitive_fee` (fee_type 118) and `other_fees` (all remaining fee types). Revenue = logistics_fee + overtime_fine + sensitive_fee + other_fees. Fees and `weight` are **maturity-gated**: immature parcels contribute 0, so the fee denominator must be `volume_mature`, not `volume`. Maturity rate = SUM(volume_mature) / SUM(volume). `volume` counts all sales tracking_ids; `volume_mature` counts only parcels whose purchase-side costs have landed. `gmv` and `mid_cnt` are **not** maturity-gated. Amounts are not FX-converted in the DAG (they follow the sales payment dump currency, typically CNY); Tableau may convert with a dashboard exchange-rate parameter. Feeds the Tableau workbook *Logistics Finance Dashboard New* (custom SQL selects the latest `dt` partition). Tableau models under `semantic_layer/models/tableau/` own any dimension joins; this wrapper performs no joins. Source: wishpost.finance_monthly_sales_breakdown_1y.

Master commerce transaction fact — one row per commerce line item for every Wish transaction, enriched with payment, shipping, tax and refund state. Physical source is the Hive table `wish.master_commerce_transactions`, produced daily by the Airflow / Spark ETL that lands MongoDB `commerce_transaction` / `commerce_transaction_item` documents. This model is a read-only view over that table (materialized in schema `semantic_dw`); the ETL is not reimplemented here.

**Grain** — one row per (transaction_id, variation_id) line item. The documented composite key is (transaction_id, variation_id), so the surrogate primary key `transaction_variation_id` is `concat(transaction_id, '-', variation_id)`.

**Order vs line grain** — one commerce transaction spans many line rows, so the transaction-level columns (`order_total`, `order_subtotal`, `order_shipping`, `tax_amount`, `tax_cost`, `tax_fee`, `processor_fee`, `cash_applied`, `discount_amount`, `discounts_applied`, `total_credits_applied`, `credits_applied`, `installments`) are *repeated on every line row* of the same transaction. Summing them over line rows over-counts by the number of lines per transaction; aggregate at `transaction_id` first when a per-transaction number is needed. The line-level columns (`paid_price`, `paid_shipping`, `item_price`, `item_total`, `cost`, `quantity`, `gmv`, `actual_gmv`) are safe to sum over line rows.

**Time** — `dt` is the Hive partition (varchar YYYY-MM-DD) and the default metric time dimension; it is the pipeline refresh date, *not* the checkout date. `transaction_create_date`, `transaction_date` and `payment_received_date` are extra day-grain time dimensions derived from the unix-second columns; the project time spine is day, so no hour/second-grain time dimension is registered. The raw unix columns are kept alongside `*_ts` timestamp columns for joins. Data is typically available with a 24-hour delay.

**Enums** — `state`, `payment_type`, `client` and `refund_reason_category` keep their raw integer code and gain a human-readable `*_name` column built from the documented code list. `app_type_name` already exists in the source and is passed through.

models.model_description:
Order tracking records for Wish shipments: one row per order-tracking record, carrying the tracking provider, the current carrier state, the shipment / delivery timestamps, the destination geography and the shipping cost / weight. Source: `wish.master_order_tracking_infos`, a Hive view over the MongoDB `sweeper__ordertrackinginfo_cow` collection that is rebuilt daily by the incremental OTI processing pipeline (`incremental_processing_oti.py`) with merge logic for updates. No Airflow / Spark ETL logic is reimplemented in this wrapper and the grain is not changed.
Partitioned by `dt` (varchar YYYY-MM-DD, cast to date here). `dt` is calculated by the source ETL from the record creation timestamp, so it is the *creation* day of the tracking record, and it is the default metric time dimension. The data has a 1-2 day freshness lag, and old partitions may be archived or deleted by the retention policy.
The physical table documents `tracking_id` as the primary key, but the table is incrementally re-emitted with merge logic, so the same `tracking_id` can reappear in a later partition. The wrapper therefore exposes the surrogate key `tracking_record_key` (`concat_ws('||', tracking_id, dt)`), which is unique at the physical grain even when `tracking_id` repeats across partitions, and keeps `tracking_id` as a join key.
Time semantics: the Unix-epoch columns documented as such (`tracking_created_time`, `confirmed_delivered_time`, `shipped_date`, `tracking_cancelled_date`, `first_confirmed_update_time`, `first_in_transit_tracking_time`, `wishpost_order_creation_time`, `time`) are converted with `from_unixtime` to `*_ts` timestamps and, where they are used as time dimensions, to `*_day` dates. The project time spine is day-grained, so only `dt`, `shipped_day` and `confirmed_delivered_day` are registered as MetricFlow time dimensions. `exp_delivery_time` is an integer "expected delivery timestamp" whose encoding the table documentation does not state as Unix seconds, so it is exposed as a raw bigint only. Timestamps are mostly UTC, though the documentation warns that some source values may be in local time zones.
PII columns (`name`, `phone_number`, `signed_by`, `street_address`) are exposed by the underlying view but are deliberately NOT declared as MetricFlow dimensions.

models.model_description:
Product-variation catalog snapshot for the Wish marketplace: one row per product variation per `dt` daily snapshot partition, carrying pricing, inventory, rating, shipping-time and catalog-state attributes plus the product / merchant / manufacturer keys. Physical source is the Hive view `wish.master_product_variations`, built daily at 02:00 UTC by the Airflow / Spark ETL that lands the MongoDB `CommerceProduct` and `CommerceVariation` collections (`IncrementalProductVariations_Tahoe`, `IncrementalProductVariations_Part2`). This model is a read-only view over that table (materialized in schema `semantic_dw`); the ETL is not reimplemented here.

**Grain** — one row per (`_id`, `dt`). The table documentation names `_id` as the primary key, but the source is a *daily full snapshot* of the catalog, so `_id` is unique only inside a partition. The wrapper therefore exposes the surrogate key `variation_snapshot_id` (`concat_ws('||', _id, dt)`) as the primary entity and keeps `_id` (exposed as `variation_id`) as a join key.

**Snapshot semantics** — every partition repeats the whole catalog, so `sum`-style metrics over `inventory` / `purchase_count` / `rating_count` are *point-in-time snapshot values*, not flows. Do not sum them across `dt` days: read them as-of a single partition. The count metrics describe the catalog of the filtered day(s).

**Time** — `dt` (varchar YYYY-MM-DD) is the Hive partition and the default metric time dimension; it is the snapshot date, not an event date, so always filter it for partition pruning. `time`, `generation_time` and `synced_time` are bigint "timestamp" columns; the raw integers are kept for joins and paired with `*_ts` timestamps and `*_date` day-grain columns. The project time spine is day, so only `dt`, `creation_date`, `generation_date` and `synced_date` are registered as MetricFlow time dimensions — no hour/second-grain time dimension is exposed.

**Enums and flags** — `review_status` keeps its numeric code and gains `review_status_name` (0=PENDING, 1=REJECTED, 2=APPROVED). The boolean-like flags (`enabled`, `halt_sales`, `is_fbw_item`, `product_removed`, `product_removed_by_merchant`, `variation_removed`, `is_unity`) are varchar `'true'` / `'false'` / null in the source; the raw column stays the filter target and each flag gains a `*_name` companion with a human-readable label. `rating_category` is the documented rating bucket (>= 4.0 HIGH, >= 3.0 MEDIUM, else LOW, null UNKNOWN).

**Caveats** — money is multi-currency: `merchant_price` and `cost` are in `merchant_source_currency` (documented default USD), the `localized_*` columns are in the localized currency, and the documented ETL falls back to the localized value when the merchant price is missing. Price / cost metrics are therefore averages over a mixed-currency population, not currency-safe totals. `inventory` is already the ETL-summarized level (the sum of the warehouse inventories when present, otherwise the raw level) and is not recomputed here. `options`, `attribute_name_to_value` and `merchant_warehouse_inventories` are JSON strings; `wish_express_countries` is a comma-separated country list, so country-level filtering on it is exact-match only.

**Dimension joins** (product, merchant, manufacturer) belong in a Tableau datasource model under `semantic_layer/models/tableau/` that `ref()`s this wrapper, not in this Hive model.

models.model_description:
Wish user master — one row per user, holding the current profile, demographic and account-status attributes for every user on the platform. The physical source is the Hive view `wish.master_users`, produced by the `IncrementalUser_Tahoe` Airflow DAG that extracts MongoDB `User` / `UserMLInfo` / `UserSignupInfo` documents. This model is a read-only view over that table (materialized in schema `semantic_dw`); the ETL is not reimplemented here.

**Grain** — one row per user. `user_id` (the Mongo `ObjectId` hex string) is the primary key and is unique across the table. The underlying object is a Hive *view* that the DAG repoints at a fresh full snapshot every night; the snapshot is built as `(previous snapshot LEFT ANTI JOIN today's changed users) UNION ALL (today's changed users)`, so it always holds every user exactly once with the freshest available profile. There is no row-level history: a user's attributes are overwritten in place on the next refresh.

**`dt` is the registration date, not the snapshot date** — the producer writes `dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(int(str(user.id)[:8], 16))`, i.e. the Mongo `ObjectId` prefix, so `dt` is immutable for a given user. It is nevertheless the physical Hive partition of the view. Practical consequences: `GROUP BY dt` is a *registration cohort* breakdown, not a daily-snapshot breakdown; the total row count of the table is the total user base (every user, forever), not "users as of the last run"; and no column identifies the snapshot date, so point-in-time (as-of) analysis is not possible on this table. `registration_date` is the UTC calendar day of the same registration instant and can differ from `dt` by one day for users registered close to midnight, because `dt` is computed in the producer's local timezone.

**Time** — `dt` is the Hive partition and the default metric time dimension. `registration_date`, `last_active_date` and `birthdate` are additional day-grain time dimensions. The project time spine is day, so no hour/second-grain time dimension is registered; the raw unix-second columns (`time`, `registration_time`, `last_active_day`) and the derived `*_ts` timestamps are kept for joins only. `last_active_date` is null for users who have never been active, and `birthdate` is null for users without a birth date — the two are populated differently, so neither is a drop-in replacement for `dt`.

**Enums** — `gender`, `age_range`, `education_level`, `relationship_status`, `signup_method` and `user_status` keep their raw integer code and gain a human-readable `*_name` column built from the documented code list. `app_name` already exists in the source (the producer maps it from `app_type` via `UserAppType`) and is passed through unchanged.

**Flags** — `is_wish_star`, `likely_bot`, `is_temporary`, `is_verified` and `is_guest_user` are varchar `'true'` / `'false'` strings in the source. The raw column is kept as a categorical dimension and a boolean `*_flag` column is added next to it, so filters can be written as `{% raw %}{{ Dimension }}{% endraw %} = true`. `is_guest_user` is marked "TODO deprecate" in the producing DAG, so it should not be relied on for reporting.

**Caveats** — the table documentation recommends filtering out `likely_bot = 'true'` users for business metrics and `is_temporary = 'true'` users for permanent-user analysis; the `bot_users` and `temporary_users` metrics quantify those populations. `email`, `full_name`, `profile_pic`, `fb_uid` and `google_plus_uid` are PII. `likely_bot` is a model output and is known to mis-flag some legitimate users. `signup_method` is partly inferred by the producer when the user has no explicit signup info, and `app_name` is derived from `app_type` rather than stored independently.

models.model_description:
Merchant-side refund line items. Grain is one row per refund item (`id`, the MongoDB `MerchantTransactionRefundItem._id` string) - one refund item belongs to one merchant transaction (`m_transaction_id`), and one merchant transaction can carry many refund items, so aggregate at `id` before joining to avoid fan-out.

The physical object is a partitioned Hive VIEW over the daily snapshot `sweeper.merchant_transaction_refund_items_YYYYMMDD`, recreated by Airflow DAG `incremental_mtrefund_tahoe` (the table doc calls it `IncrementalMTRefund_Tahoe`). The DAG extracts the MongoDB `MerchantTransaction.refund_items` sub-documents for the run-day window, merges them into the previous master and keeps the newest version of each `id` (`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY dt DESC)`). The wrapper materializes as a view in `semantic_dw`, so `wish.merchant_transaction_refund_items` is never overwritten.

Time semantics: `dt` (varchar YYYY-MM-DD, cast to DATE here) is the ETL **load / change day** of the row version, NOT the business day of the refund. The upstream ETL is a MongoDB change-data-capture merge, so a refund item that is edited upstream is re-emitted into a later `dt` partition. `dt` is the default metric time dimension and drives partition pruning; always filter it. `refund_date` is the business refund day (the UTC calendar day of the refund creation) and is the correct axis for refund-day reporting. `merchant_payment_date` is the business day the merchant payout was deducted. The refund-leg status change days (`payment_refund_status_date`, `cash_refund_status_date`), the legacy non-ISO `refunded_date` rendering and the `time` / `time_ts` ETL load-window marker are kept as plain columns - the project time spine is day, and only `dt`, `refund_date` and `merchant_payment_date` are registered as MetricFlow time dimensions.

Amounts: every amount column in this table is in the **original (merchant) currency**, not USD - `amount`, `refund_payment_amount`, `refund_cash_amount`, `refund_credit_amount` are in the transaction currency, and `merchant_amount` / `merchant_responsible_amount` are in the merchant source currency (the ETL writes the *localized* merchant cost basis, not the USD one). There is no USD-normalized amount column on this table. Read the amount metrics per currency - use `merchant_source_currency` / `merchant_currency_code` / `authority_currency_code` to slice - or within a single merchant. The `localized_*` columns are the buyer's local-currency counterparts and are deliberately not exposed as metrics because they are not aggregatable across currencies.

Enums: `source`, `type`, `amount_type`, `refund_payment_method` and `merchant_payment_status` keep their raw code and gain a human-readable `*_name` column. `payment_refund_status` and `cash_refund_status` already carry the readable text produced by the ETL (`Pending` / `Confirmed` / `Not Paid` / `Denied`).

Known gaps carried from the source: `net_tax`, `sales_tax` and the three `*_in_merchant_currency` tax columns are deprecated and are not populated by the current ETL (always NULL for rows it writes), so they are exposed for lineage but carry no metric. `reason_id` has no name column on this table - use `reason_text` and join `sweeper_dev.dim_refund_reasons` in a Tableau model if the code list is needed. `source` has no documented code list in the table doc; the `source_name` mapping follows the `RefundSource` enum in `clroot/sweeper/model/commerce_transaction_refund.py`, and `source_text` is the ETL's context-aware rendering, which can be more specific than `source_name` (e.g. "Refunded by Wish Assistant").

models.model_description:
Current-state master record of every merchant user account on the Wish marketplace. One row per account: the Mongo `ObjectId` hex string in `id` is the primary key, and the producing dump de-duplicates on it (`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY id)`) before it writes `wish.merchant_user`.
The physical object is a Hive table over the MongoDB `sweeper-merchant` `MerchantUser` collection, refreshed every day at 00:00 UTC by the Airflow DAG `MerchantUserDump`. It is NOT partitioned and carries no snapshot-date column, so there is no partition time dimension. The default `agg_time_dimension` is `onboarding_completed_calendar_date` -- the merchant onboarding-completion day -- which is a COHORT anchor, not a snapshot day: grouping by it answers "merchant users that finished onboarding that day". Accounts that never finished onboarding have a NULL date and are therefore dropped from a time-bucketed query; use `last_active_calendar_date` when the intent is recency instead.
This is an account dimension, not an event log: every row carries the account state as of the last successful daily dump. The account-level counters (`num_noti_attention`, `emails_sent`, `phone_calls_made`, `sms_codes_sent`, `sms_validation_attempts`, `tfa_attempts`) and the monetary snapshots (`annual_gmv`, `preorder_gmv`) are as-of-dump values and are NOT additive over time -- summing them across dates double counts the same account. `rev_share` and `erp_promo_rev_share` are rates (percent, 0-100) and must be averaged, not summed.

models.model_description:
Daily full snapshot of the Wish merchant dimension, one row per merchant (`merchant_id`, the Mongo `ObjectId` hex string). The underlying physical object `wish.dim_all_merchants` is a Hive external Parquet table in S3, rebuilt every day at 03:00 America/Los_Angeles by the Airflow DAG `DailyIncrementalMerchants`, which writes a temp table and atomically swaps it into place. Consumers therefore always see the latest snapshot; there is no history in this table.
The table consolidates `wish.commerce_merchant` and `wish.merchant_user` attributes and adds channel / priority metadata plus rule-based business labels (`segment`, `wish_priority`, `from_trusted_channel`, `is_deliverr_merchant`, `group_name_en`, `signup_source`).
The table is NOT partitioned -- `SHOW CREATE TABLE` declares no partition column -- so there is no partition time dimension and no `is_partition` marker here. The closest analogue to a partition is the `time` column (the ingestion-time epoch written by the producer DAG at run time), exposed as `snapshot_ts` / `snapshot_date`. It is constant for the whole snapshot: it answers "which daily snapshot did this row come from", NOT "when did something happen to this merchant". Grouping by it is therefore useless for trends.
The default `agg_time_dimension` is `reg_date` -- the merchant registration day derived from the `ObjectId` prefix (`CONV(SUBSTRING(merchant_id, 1, 8), 16, 10)`). It is a cohort anchor and, unlike `approved_calendar_date`, it is populated for every row, so a time-bucketed query does not silently drop merchants that are not approved yet. Use `approved_calendar_date` (approval cohort), `disable_calendar_date` (disable cohort), `onboarding_completed_calendar_date` (onboarding cohort) or `bba_approved_calendar_date` (blanket-auth approval cohort) when that is the intent -- those are NULL for the rows they do not apply to.
This is a merchant dimension, not an event log: every row carries the merchant's state as of the last successful daily build. The merchant counters (`num_active_products`, `rating_count`, `rating_count_14_days`) and the quality rates (`average_rating`, `average_rating_14_days`, `rev_share`) are as-of-snapshot values and are NOT additive over time -- summing them across dates double counts the same merchant. `rev_share` and the ratings are rates: average them, do not sum them.
Data quality: the producer DAG runs a duplicate check on `merchant_id` (`IncMerchantsDuplicateValidate`) and alerts when the duplicate count is greater than zero, so `merchant_id` is expected to be unique and non-null. Boolean-like fields are stored as strings (`'true'` / `'false'` for the CASE-generated `from_trusted_channel` and `is_deliverr_merchant`), so consumers must normalize explicitly. `segment` and `wish_priority` are rule-based and may change whenever the upstream logic changes. `signup_source` defaults to `'Organic'` when the source value is null.
PII columns (personal names, e-mail, phone numbers, street addresses) are exposed by the underlying table and by this view, but are deliberately NOT exposed as MetricFlow dimensions.
Source: documentation/llm_generated/hive/wish/dim_all_merchants.md

metrics.metric_description: Last-mile cost allocated to the combined shipment: large cargo + logistics + warehouse + VAT + volumetric + other allocated purchase fees.

metrics.evidence: First-mile total sale fees minus total purchase fees is sum_fm profit.
metrics.metric_description: First-mile P&L: total sale fees minus total purchase fees. Flattened from the simple fee metrics so no derived metric depends on another derived metric. Excludes the last-mile allocated purchase cost (`total_purchase_fee_post`). Can be negative (losses).

metrics.evidence: GMV over distinct tracking_id is atv.avg_per_parcel.
metrics.metric_description: GMV divided by the number of distinct parcels in scope. NULL when there are no parcels in the selection.

metrics.evidence: Numerator/denominator flat-rate ratio matches flat_rate_coefficient.
metrics.metric_description: Flat-rate shipping coefficient: numerator divided by denominator. NULL when the denominator is zero.

metrics.evidence: First-mile profit over total sale fees matches fm_total_fees.
metrics.metric_description: First-mile profit divided by total sale fees (0.2 = 20% margin). Derived from the simple fee metrics of the same model; inherits the snapshot caveat of its inputs - filter to a single `dt` partition for a point-in-time number.

metrics.evidence: delivered_parcels / parcels on WishPost snapshots is parcel_delivery_rate.
metrics.metric_description: Share of parcels in scope that reached the delivered last-mile checkpoint. Matches the documented `SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_ts IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)` (as a fraction, not a percentage).

models.model_description: WishPost logistics order fact covering the complete parcel lifecycle, from first-mile pickup through last-mile delivery, with the commerce and China payment finance rollups attached. Grain is one row per first-mile WishPost parcel (`tracking_id`) per `dt` snapshot partition. Built by the Airflow DAG `dag_tahoe_wosp_order_clean_full_cycle` (task `full_cycle_query`, daily 09:00 Asia/Shanghai). The task LEFT JOINs `wishpost.tmp_wishpost_order_clean_with_finance` (first-mile rows, `combined_to <> 'None'`) to the combined-program rows of the same table on `pre.combined_to = post.id`, and UNION ALLs the standalone rows (`combined_to = 'None'`). The optional last-mile shipment is therefore exposed through the `*_post` columns, and the parcel's share of the combined shipment's weight through `weight_proportion`. IMPORTANT - `dt` is a snapshot ("as of") date, not the order date: the upstream `wishpost.wishpost_order_clean` keeps a rolling ~200-day window of orders per partition (`order_created_time >= unix_timestamp(ds - 200 days)`), so every parcel re-appears in up to ~200 consecutive `dt` partitions. Summing an additive measure over more than one `dt` value counts each parcel once per partition it appears in. `dt` is the default metric time dimension; use `order_created_day` (or the other journey `*_day` columns) for business-date cuts, and restrict to a single `dt` for snapshot-scoped ("as of") reporting. All `bigint` time columns are Unix epoch seconds: the raw integer is kept for joins, and a `*_at` timestamp plus a `*_day` calendar date are added for the day-granularity time dimensions (the project time spine is day). `time` is the Spark load instant and must never be used as a business filter. Money columns are swept per `tracking_id` from `wish.fact_trans_detail` and are not FX-converted upstream; the finance step applies the documented currency conversion (USD x 6.5, ZAR x 0.45). This wrapper performs no joins. Tableau models under `semantic_layer/models/tableau/` own the dimension joins (channel, warehouse, pricing program) and `ref()` this model. Materialized as a view in `semantic_dw`; the physical Hive table is never modified.
